acme-sre: Hey team — since ~09:22 PST we've been getting a spike of 502/504s to Redwood hosted API for our inference calls. Correlation IDs: 0ab3f7.., 0ab3f8.., looks like TLS handshake timeouts to api.redwood.com:443. Started right after your scheduled cert rotation? Can you help investigate?

jordan: on it. can you paste a failing curl -v (or the client TLS error) and the IP you resolve for api.redwood.com from your VPC?

acme-sre: here's a failing curl from their app host (stripped keys):

```
$ curl -v https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate 
*   Trying 198.51.100.23:443...
* connect to 198.51.100.23 port 443 failed: Operation timed out
* Failed to connect to api.redwood.example port 443: Operation timed out
* Closing connection 0
curl: (28) Connection timed out after 10001 milliseconds

TLS log from client: tls: handshake timeout
```

acme-sre: dig from the same host returns 198.51.100.23 (short TTL 30s). traceroute shows a couple of hops timing out occasionally.

marie: I see a cert-rollout job kicked off at 2026-03-10T09:21:12Z in Deploy. rollout-id: ro-78f2. deploy-bot posted a note: "cert-rotation: started -> edge pool A,B,C".

deploy-bot: cert-rotation ro-78f2 status: in-progress -> applied to pool A at 09:21:12Z, pool B at 09:21:24Z, pool C at 09:21:35Z.

ravi: @marie @jordan could this be a resolver/egress path flap during the rollout? We had an earlier incident where short DNS TTL + simultaneous route changes caused TCP handshake drops.

marie: running `dig +short @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example` from one of our probes: returns 198.51.100.23 then 203.0.113.9 (rotation). Doing `dig +trace` shows intermittent SERVFAIL from the customer's recursive at ~09:22:30.

jordan: can you capture a tcpdump from a customer host or our edge talking to that IP? specifically looking for SYN retransmits and RSTs. Also share the customer NAT/conntrack counts.

acme-sre: attached tcpdump excerpt (pasted):
```
09:22:34.123456 IP 10.0.0.5.54012 > 198.51.100.23.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460,sackOK,TS val 123456 ecr 0], length 0
09:22:44.123789 IP 10.0.0.5.54012 > 198.51.100.23.443: Flags [S], seq 0, retransmission, length 0
09:22:54.124012 IP 10.0.0.5.54012 > 198.51.100.23.443: Flags [S], seq 0, retransmission, length 0

no SYN/ACK ever seen back.
```

ravi: that pattern matches an egress path blackhole or a rate-limited upstream appliance. Also suspicious that the IP flips during the same TTL window. Could be a resolver returning multiple A records where only some paths are healthy right now.

marie: checking our egress logs — connections to 198.51.100.23 from edge POOL-B show a 40% SYN timeout rate between 09:21:50-09:23:10. Pool-A and Pool-C lower but non-zero.

ops-bot: dns-change: zone api.redwood.example had an authoritative NS update at 2026-03-10T09:20:59Z (propagation in progress).

jordan: hypothesis: cert rotation + authoritative NS change + short TTL caused a partial DNS fanout: some clients got new IPs pointing at edge instances that were in mid-rotate and briefly dropped packets, leading to handshake timeouts. Workarounds: 1) client-side: retry with multiple A records; 2) temporary routing fallback on our side to healthy pools; 3) increase DNS TTL for rotation windows.

marie: agree. immediate mitigation: enable automatic fallback routing for requests that hit handshake timeouts — route to backup pool D which still has pre-rotation certs until rollout completes. I'm pushing a route update now.

deploy-bot: traffic-route update tr-554 applied: route TLS handshake failure fallback -> pool-D at 09:28:01Z.

acme-sre: after ~09:29 our errors dropped to normal. Latency is back to baseline. Thanks. We'll keep an eye and re-open if it recurs.

jordan: can you confirm customer saw success? any residual errors?

acme-sre: confirmed — error rate back to 0.1% from 8%. not reproducible anymore.

ravi: follow-ups: (1) run a short audit on cert-rotation orchestration to avoid draining + DNS NS update in same window; (2) recommend TTL bump during future rotations to 300s; (3) add observability for SYN timeout spikes per-edge IP during rollouts. I'll file follow-up tickets.

marie: filing ENG tickets now and tagging oncall for a postmortem. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:

jordan: summary for support ticket SR-2026-8712: customer reported TLS handshake timeouts => root cause partial egress path failures during cert rotation + NS update causing DNS fanout to mixed pools. Mitigation: route fallback to pool-D applied, errors resolved. Next actions: orchestration change + TTL guidance.

acme-sre: appreciate the fast response — please send the postmortem link when ready.

marie: will do, linking here when available.
